hook.text: Those tall steel towers carry power at hundreds of thousands of volts.

buildup.text: High voltage keeps current low. Low current means less energy wasted as heat.

discovery.text: Power loss equals I²R — halve the current and you cut losses to one quarter.

twist.text: Air itself can break down and arc at very high voltage. Insulators must be massive.

climax.text: Ultra-high voltage lines at 1,100 kV span thousands of kilometers in China.

punchline.text: Higher voltage, lower current, less waste — simple physics, huge savings.

quiz.question: Why are transmission lines operated at very high voltage?
options: High voltage makes electricity travel faster through the wires
Less current flows, reducing I²R heat losses dramatically
High voltage prevents lightning from striking the lines
